def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a basic regex matching algorithm using recursion and backtracking
    to support literal characters, '.', '*', and '+'.
    """
    
    def is_match(p: str, t: str) -> bool:
        # Base case: if the pattern is empty, the text should also be empty
        if not p:
            return not t
        
        # First match condition: check if the first characters match
        first_match = bool(t) and (p[0] == t[0] or p[0] == '.')
        
        # Handle '*' operator
        if len(p) >= 2 and p[1] == '*':
            # Try to match zero occurrences or one or more occurrences
            return (is_match(p[2:], t) or
                    (first_match and is_match(p, t[1:])))
        
        # Handle '+' operator
        elif len(p) >= 2 and p[1] == '+':
            # Must have at least one occurrence of the preceding element
            return (first_match and 
                    (is_match(p[2:], t[1:]) or is_match(p, t[1:])))
        
        # Proceed with normal matching if no special characters
        return first_match and is_match(p[1:], t[1:])

    return is_match(pattern, text)
